### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

**Charter-global conclusions this task rests on are cited, not restated.** See
`env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/air_ticketing_desk/_difficulty.md`:
§ `policy_conflict_scan` (base section verbatim, subjects and gates), § `rule_compute_equivalence`,
§ `action_binding_and_uuids` (uuid8s, docstring silence, and the function-body citation that no tool
judges a prerequisite), § `prerequisite_graph`, § `prerequisite_sentences`,
§ `override_declarations` and § `factor_ladders`.

**Handling time.** Every formula of this task was evaluated on `initial_state` plus the preceding
synchronous writes at its own write step, and each problem's moment is after all of its own
prerequisites are resolved and before it is itself written:

- `air_ext_cancellation_penalty` and `air_ext_airline_tax_return` have `prerequisite: []` and are
  evaluated on the opening world.
- `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` is evaluated on the opening world **plus** the penalty line and
  the tax payout line, which is exactly what its `penalty_withheld` and `returned_to_card` bindings
  read.
- `air_ext_pooled_credit_release` is evaluated on that world **plus** the credit issue line, which is
  what its `pool_issued` binding reads.

No later write is computed early: the three later values each change when an earlier write is
skipped, as shown in `problem_chain`. Neither the persona nor a tool fallback substitutes for an
eligibility judgement anywhere — the persona states no amount and no rule (see
`task_independent_derivation`).

**Parallel-edge order.** `air_ext_cancellation_penalty` and `air_ext_airline_tax_return` are
siblings under `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` with no edge between them, and both read an
unfiltered `SUM('air_booking_events','amount_usd')` as a cap (`ticket_value` and `money_collected`
respectively), so each write moves the other's cap. The order is therefore only immaterial if
neither cap binds, and on this world neither does: the penalty cap is `3663.10 − 24.95 × 2 =
3613.20` against a penalty of `114.19`, and the tax-return cap is `3663.10` (or `3777.29` if the
penalty is posted first) against a return of `661.81`. Recomputing with the opposite order gives the
identical pair of values. **No second terminal state arises from the order.** The dependence is
nevertheless real and is recorded as charter observation CG-6 in `_difficulty.md`.

**Real-world waits.** Every fact a gold write consumes is either an authoritative record already in
`initial_state` (the fare, tax, service-fee, ancillary, change-fee and notice rows; the approved
`refund_review`; the club card and its points ledger; the linked care policy) or the real DB effect
of a preceding write of this same task. Nothing waits on a diagnosis, a delivery, a clearing, a
manual approval, a batch, a future date or a cooling-off period. The booking already stands at
`cancelled` with an **approved** refund review on file, so the base gates
`air_cancel_refund.refund_review_approved`, `air_credit_validity.cancelled_before_issue` and
`air_refund_settlement.refund_stage_reached` are all satisfied at the opening without waiting.
**PASS.**

**Consequences of the charter-global defects on this task's world.**

*CG-1 (undeclared override of `air_evt_schedule_change_rights`) — demonstrated here.* The booking
carries `air_booking_events.0960d251…`, an `air_schedule_change_notice` of
`schedule_change_minutes: 155` posted `2026-05-14`. Economy Classic's
`schedule_change_threshold_minutes` is `120`, so `155 ≥ 120`: this is a move at or beyond the
brand's threshold. The inherited base sentence gives Priya the right *"to be refunded in full to the
original form of payment whatever the brand's ordinary refund form"* — that is, `3663.10` to her card
and no penalty withheld. The extended tree instead withholds `114.19`, returns `661.81` to the card
and puts `2433.49` on a voucher. Both readings are defensible from the charter as it stands, and they
differ in form (card vs voucher), in amount and in whether a penalty exists at all. The persona even
supplies the trigger in her own words — *"a trip to Tokyo that the airline kept moving around"*.
**SOURCE-POLICY RED, demonstrated.**

*CG-2 (undeclared override of `air_baggage_fee`) — demonstrated here.* The booking carries one
optional extra, `fee6852a…`, `air_ancillary_charge / checked_bag`, `amount_usd 45.00`, posted
`2026-06-02`. The cancellation is outside the 24-hour void window (`ticketed_at 2026-04-11 16:42`,
`cancelled_at 2026-07-20 15:03`) and no notice on the booking records that the flight did not
operate (all three notices carry `reason_code: involuntary_schedule_change`), so base refunds this
bag line in **no** amount. `air_ext_airline_tax_return` nonetheless adds `45.00 × 0.5 = 22.50` to the
cash payout (declared override), and `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` adds a further
`45.00 × 0.5 = 22.50` to the voucher (**undeclared**). The traveller recovers `45.00` of a `45.00`
charge, half as money and half as credit. **SOURCE-POLICY RED, demonstrated.**

*CG-3 (undeclared override of `air_club_benefit_interaction`) — demonstrated here.* Priya holds an
active Gold card enrolled `2016-11-03`, i.e. `MONTHS('2016-11-03','2026-09-17') = 118` months, which
is inside `long_membership_months = 120`, so `member_voucher_uplift` takes its third tier,
`entry_member_uplift = 0.02`. That multiplies the voucher by `1.02`, converting the club tier into
`2806.795 × 0.02 = 56.14` before the protection offset, and `2433.49 − 2385.78 = 47.71` of scored
voucher value — precisely what base forbids with *"the club benefit is not converted into value"*,
and a use of the tier that base does not list among the two things the tier decides. Substituting the
base sentence gives a voucher of `2385.78` instead of `2433.49`.
**SOURCE-POLICY RED, demonstrated.**

*CG-4 (two writes bring the waited-on state about).* On **this** world the ambiguity does not by
itself leave the agent stranded: `air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward` presupposes vouchers already
standing lapsed on the booking, and `e7060f7c…` carries no `air_credit_issue` row at all
(`credit_balance_usd: 0.0`), so its rule cannot fire and a careful reader is left with
`issue_travel_credit_voucher_dd7ecc26` as the only write that can produce the state. The defect is
therefore recorded at charter level with its consequence for the reader, and this task's tree is
resolvable. Carried as the charter finding, not as a second task-level red light.

*CG-7 (mislabelled `method` factors).* Demonstrated on this task's computations in `factor_weight`.

### problem_chain

Walked out from the root problem using the policy and the world alone, without reading
`prerequisite_closure`.

**Root.** Priya asks for one thing: *"I'd like whatever is left from the Tokyo ticket put toward the
Lisbon flight I'm holding."* That is the subject of `air_ext_pooled_credit_release` — value released
from the pooled travel credit onto an unticketed itinerary the traveller is holding. Its
`target_tool` is `release_travel_credit_value_2b680572`, `owner="user"`.

**Hop 1.** `air_ext_pooled_credit_release.rule` carries one prerequisite sentence: *"Value is
released from the traveller's pooled travel credit only after a travel credit voucher stands issued
against the cancelled booking."* Is that state true at `frozen_time`? **No.** There is no
`air_credit_issue` row anywhere in `initial_state.air_booking_events` (all 13 rows are
`air_fare_charge` ×6, `air_change_fee_charge` ×3, `air_schedule_change_notice` ×3,
`air_ancillary_charge` ×1), and `air_bookings.e7060f7c….credit_balance_usd` is `0.0`. Reading the
other policies' rules for the one whose result is a voucher issued against a cancelled booking gives
`air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` ("The value placed on the voucher is the fare, tax and service
lines collected on the booking…"), resolved by `issue_travel_credit_voucher_dd7ecc26`.

**Hop 2.** `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit.rule` carries two prerequisite sentences:

- *"The value placed on the voucher is fixed only after the cancellation penalty owed under the fare
  brand held stands as a withheld line on the booking."* True at `frozen_time`? **No** — there is no
  `air_penalty_charge` row on `e7060f7c…`. The policy whose result is that withheld penalty is
  `air_ext_cancellation_penalty`, resolved by `withhold_cancellation_penalty_77ca3b84`.
- *"The value placed on the voucher is fixed only after the taxes and carrier fees the airline
  returns stand as a payout line on the booking."* True at `frozen_time`? **No** — there is no
  `air_refund_payout` row on `e7060f7c…`. The policy whose result is that payout is
  `air_ext_airline_tax_return`, resolved by `return_airline_refunded_taxes_4767edfd`.

**Hop 3.** Both of those policies declare `prerequisite: []`, and neither rule carries a sentence
saying its own result waits on anything. The walk terminates.

**Derived tree** (identical in shape to the author's `prerequisite` declarations):

```
air_ext_pooled_credit_release                (root; owner=user)
  └─ value_input ─> air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit
                      ├─ value_input ─> air_ext_cancellation_penalty
                      └─ value_input ─> air_ext_airline_tax_return
```

- n = **3** prerequisite problems (inside the permitted 1–3).
- **3** `value_input` edges ≥ `max(n − 1, 1) = 2`. **PASS.**
- No cycle. **PASS.**
- Topological order: `{air_ext_cancellation_penalty, air_ext_airline_tax_return}` (either order, see
  `policy_self_consistency`) → `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` → `air_ext_pooled_credit_release`.
- A customer's own write is in the tree: the root is `release_travel_credit_value_2b680572`,
  `@tool(owner="user", …)`, and the persona hands it over passively at the agent's direction —
  *"When the agent tells her the value is ready and hands her the step to release it herself, she
  says 'right, let me do that' and runs it."* **PASS.**

**DB row evidence per edge for "why it is false at the opening":** given above — absence of any
`air_penalty_charge`, `air_refund_payout` and `air_credit_issue` row on `e7060f7c…`, corroborated by
`credit_balance_usd: 0.0`. None of the three edges is an eligibility that is already satisfied.

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (skip the depended-on write, replay everything else, recompute):

| edge skipped | binding that loses its value | recomputed downstream value | gold-path value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| penalty → credit | `penalty_withheld` 114.19 → 0, so `penalty_deduction` 57.095 → 0 | voucher 2433.49 → **2482.99**, release 1161.29 → **1183.59** | 2433.49 / 1161.29 |
| tax return → credit | `returned_to_card` 661.81 → 0 | voucher 2433.49 → **3007.28**, release 1161.29 → **1419.78** | 2433.49 / 1161.29 |
| credit → release | `pool_issued` 2433.49 → 0, so `open_pool` → 0 | release 1161.29 → **65.00** | 1161.29 |

Every edge changes a scored parameter. **No decorative dependency. PASS.**

**Parallel edges and the terminal state.** Argued in `policy_self_consistency`: the two sibling
writes touch one another only through caps that do not bind on this world, and both orders give
`(114.19, 661.81)`. One terminal state. **PASS.**

**No-wait argument.** Given in `policy_self_consistency`. Each resolving action is a single
synchronous tool call whose effect is a row the next step reads. **PASS.**

**The tool layer does not judge the prerequisites.** Cited from `_difficulty.md`
§ `action_binding_and_uuids`: each of the four function bodies in `task_tools.py` used by this tree
performs one unconditional `ctx.make_id` / `ctx.find` / `ctx.create` and returns a confirmation
string; there is no conditional, no raise and no hint anywhere in them, so calling
`issue_travel_credit_voucher_dd7ecc26` before the penalty line exists would succeed silently. The
decision stays with the agent. **PASS.**

**Isomorphism.** The tree derived here from the policy and the world alone has the same nodes, the
same three edges, the same `kind` on each and the same topological order as the author's
`prerequisite` declarations read in `air.extended.yaml`.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** All base eligibility holds at `frozen_time` (see
`policy_self_consistency`). Nothing in the tree waits on a future condition, and nothing in the
request falls in the charter's uncovered ground — this is not statutory delay compensation, not a
commercial-waiver request, not a compassionate refund on a nothing-back brand, not a party at or
above `group_booking_min_pax` (10 for Economy Classic; `passenger_count` is 2), and not a ticket
bought elsewhere. No `POLICY_NOT_COVERED` handoff. **Act now.**

**The user's need, authorisation and timing.** Object: the value left on the cancelled Tokyo booking
(`e7060f7c…`, which she cannot name — *"She does not remember the Tokyo locator and says so
plainly"*, so the agent looks it up by customer), to be put against the held Lisbon booking, which
she names by locator `RB9V4H` = `c3568753…`. Timing: on this call — *"she would like it done on this
call rather than being told to wait for a letter"*. Authorisation: split, and stated explicitly —
*"She is happy for the agent to do whatever the desk itself has to do on her behalf … but she is
clear that anything that is hers to sign off she will do herself there and then"*. That is exactly
the agent/user split the tree requires, and it is derivable without the agent's convenience being
used to infer anything. **The persona raises only the root problem**: it names no penalty, no tax
return and no voucher, and it never asks whether something must be sorted out first — its
conditional is passive and content-free (*"If the agent explains that something has to be settled or
recorded on the old Tokyo booking before the value can be worked out, she does not query it … She
does not suggest anything herself and does not ask what the steps are"*). It issues no second item
of work. It closes where the tree closes: *"Once she hears that the value has gone onto the Lisbon
booking, she is satisfied"*. **PASS.**

**Context closure.** Identity: name, then mobile `3122074815`, then passport last-4 `1043`, then
postal code `60614`, then DOB `1984-03-22`, one at a time as asked — all four match the `customers`
row, so `find_customers` → `verify_traveller_identity` closes. Every policy input is reachable
through a shared read tool: `find_air_bookings(customer_id=…)` for both bookings,
`find_air_booking_events(air_booking_id=…)` for the 13 ledger rows,
`find_air_service_requests(…)` for the approved review, `find_club_memberships(customer_id=…)` and
`find_club_points_entries(customer_id=…)` for the club tier and its ledger, and
`find_care_policies(linked_air_booking_id=…)` for the protection policy. Every query parameter comes
from earlier reachable information. No field needed for the answer is visible only in the raw seed.
The persona has a definite answer for everything a real agent must ask, and never supplies a policy
judgement, a calculation or a figure — *"She does not know any amounts at all … she would only be
guessing and would rather the desk read it off the record"*. **PASS.**

## findings

**F0-1 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED (a false assertion in the proof).**
*Symptom.* `prerequisite_closure` states a replay figure that recomputation contradicts.
*Root cause.* The skipped-penalty replay was carried through to the voucher correctly and then
mis-propagated to the release.
*Evidence.* `tasks/0.json` → `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect`: *"Skipping
the penalty write and replaying everything else moves the voucher value from 2433.49 to 2482.99, and
the value released from 1161.29 to 1185.02."* Recomputing on the world that sentence names for itself:
with no penalty line, `penalty_withheld = 0.00` and `penalty_deduction = 0.00`, so
`residual_value = 3553.10 − 661.81 − 49.90 − 0.00 = 2841.39` and
`voucher = RND((2841.39 + 22.50) × 1.02 × 0.85, 2) = 2482.99` — which the sentence gets right. The
release then follows `result: RND(MX(open_pool × named_share × journey_share × (1 + release_bonus) +
correction_carry, 0), 2)` = `RND(2482.99 × 0.50 × 0.85 × 1.06 + 65.00, 2)` = `RND(1183.586995, 2)` =
**1183.59**, not 1185.02. The stated figure implies an open pool of 2486.17, which no replay of this
world produces. `design_rationale`'s own per-edge sensitivity list gives the voucher figure and
declines to give a release figure, so the two proof fields do not agree with one another either.
*Demonstrated consequence.* The artifact's proof that the penalty edge bears weight asserts a value
the artifact's own compute does not produce. The edge's load-bearing conclusion survives
recomputation (1183.59 ≠ 1161.29), so the relationship holds; what fails is the proof submitted for
it, which is what an audit verifies.
*Affected artifact.* `env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/air_ticketing_desk/tasks/0.json`,
`prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect`.
*Relation to previous revisions.* First revision of this audit; no prior finding.

**F0-2 — SOURCE-POLICY RED.** The consequence of charter finding **CG-1** on this world: the
155-minute notice `0960d251…` is at or beyond Economy Classic's 120-minute threshold, so the
inherited base sentence of `air_evt_schedule_change_rights` entitles the traveller to a full refund to
the card with no penalty, while the extended tree withholds 114.19 and returns the balance as a
voucher. Evidence, consequence and locations in `policy_self_consistency` above and in
`_difficulty.md` § `findings` CG-1. *Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**F0-3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED.** The consequence of **CG-2**: the 45.00 bag line `fee6852a…`, which base
`air_baggage_fee` refunds in no amount outside the void window on a flight that operated, is returned
as 22.50 of cash and a further 22.50 of voucher value, the second undeclared. See
`policy_self_consistency` and `_difficulty.md` § `findings` CG-2. *First revision.*

**F0-4 — SOURCE-POLICY RED.** The consequence of **CG-3**: the Gold card is converted into 47.71 of
scored voucher value through `member_voucher_uplift`, against base
`air_club_benefit_interaction`'s *"the club benefit is not converted into value"*, undeclared. See
`policy_self_consistency` and `_difficulty.md` § `findings` CG-3. *First revision.*

**F0-5 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED.** The consequence of **CG-7**: counting only factors whose tiers change
how the quantity is computed, `air_ext_airline_tax_return`, `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` and
`air_ext_pooled_credit_release` each declare **zero** `method` factors against a floor of one, and
all three are computations of this task. `design_rationale`'s own factor card confirms the labels
under audit ("optional_extras_treatment (method, multi-source)", "party_charging_basis (method)",
"airline_disruption_transform (method)"). Per-computation evidence in `factor_weight`; charter-level
statement in `_difficulty.md` § `findings` CG-7. *First revision.*

**F0-6 — Observation.** The consequence of **CG-9** on this world: `journey_staleness_share` takes
15% off the releasable pool because the Tokyo departure date passed 38 days ago, although the voucher
minted at step 3 does not expire until 2027-09-17. `1354.75 − 1161.29 = 193.46` of the traveller's
own credit is withheld on a ground the base charter answers through the expiry term instead. Recorded
as an observation, not a red light: the tier is fully stated, rests on seeded records and changes the
scored number. *First revision.*

**F0-7 — Observation.** `air_ext_pooled_credit_release` releases `open_pool × 0.50` because the
cancelled booking carried two base-fare lines, yet the voucher it draws on was minted as a **single**
voucher in the caller's name for the whole party's residual value (`passenger_sequence 1`,
`voucher_value_usd 2433.49`, which nets both travellers' fares, both tax lines and both service
fees). The half that is not released is attributed to no one. Base `air_agg_credit_pooling` keeps it
on the voucher (*"the remainder stays on the last voucher touched"*), so it is not destroyed, and the
override is declared; recorded as an observation on the coherence of issuing one party-wide voucher
and then releasing it per traveller. *First revision.*

problem's moment is after all of its own prerequisites are resolved and before it is itself written.

sibling writes coupled through an unfiltered `SUM('air_booking_events','amount_usd')` cap, and order
independence had to be argued from the caps not binding. The CG-6 fix removes the coupling in one

payout — an `air_refund_payout` row — cannot enter it at all, and writing the tax return first cannot
move the penalty by any amount. In the other direction `air_ext_airline_tax_return.money_collected`
does include `air_penalty_charge`, so writing the penalty first raises its cap from 3663.10 to
3868.64; the cap does not bind against a return of 674.31 either way. Both orders give
`(205.54, 674.31)`. **One terminal state.**

**Real-world waits.** Unchanged and re-verified: every fact consumed is an authoritative record in
`initial_state` or the DB effect of a preceding write of this task. The booking stands at `cancelled`
with an approved `refund_review` decided `2026-07-27`, so `refund_review_approved`,
`cancelled_before_issue` and `refund_stage_reached` all hold at the opening; the voucher minted at
step 3 is dated `2026-09-17` with a 12-month term, so `credit_still_valid` holds for the step-4
release. Nothing waits on a clearing, an approval, a batch or a date. **PASS.**

**Consequences of the charter-global findings on this world.**

*CG-2 and CG-3 — closed, and closed on this world.* The bag line `fee6852a…` (45.00) can no longer
reach the voucher: policy 3 has no extras binding at all, so the revision-1 double return is gone —
the 45.00 charge now comes back once, through policy 2, and at the first-checked-bag rate rather than
as a half share. The Gold card still lifts the voucher by 2%, but that uplift is now a **declared**
override of `air_club_benefit_interaction` naming the verbatim base sentence, so the agent reading
base and extended together finds one rule in force, not two.

*CG-1 — NOT closed, and it is this world that demonstrates it.* Charter statement in
`_difficulty.md` § `findings (revision 2)`, CG-1. Here is the demonstration on task 0:

The booking carries three airline notices — `605b9aff…` 70 minutes, `a1aefdc0…` 45 minutes and
`0960d251…` **95** minutes — so `largest_move_minutes = 95`, below Economy Classic's
`schedule_change_threshold_minutes` of 120 and above zero. The reworked seed therefore lands the
ladder squarely on its **second** tier: `disruption_share = 0.90`.

Base `air_evt_schedule_change_rights` legislates for exactly this case and says the opposite: *"A
move smaller than the brand's threshold gives no right: a traveller who still wants to move pays the
brand's disruption rebooking fee, and a traveller who still wants to cancel is treated as a voluntary
cancellation."* Priya is a traveller who cancelled. Base treats her as an ordinary voluntary
cancellation — the sub-threshold move confers nothing. Extended reduces her penalty by a tenth
**because** that sub-threshold move stands on the booking. No `overwrite` in any of the six policies
names `air_evt_schedule_change_rights`, so both sentences are in force.

Two defensible answers on this world, and the disagreement is now load-bearing rather than latent:

| | base reading (no right from a sub-threshold move) | extended ladder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disruption_share` | 1.00 | 0.90 |
| `penalty_amount_usd` | **228.38** | **205.54** |
| `voucher_value_usd` | 2353.64 | 2363.55 |
| `released_credit_usd` | 1125.31 | 1129.78 |

Moving the notice from 155 to 95 did close revision 1's demonstration — a ≥threshold move no longer
exists on this booking, so the base sentence about a full refund to the card no longer engages, and
the revision-1 evidence would not reproduce. It did not close the finding, because the base rule
legislates for sub-threshold moves in its very next clause and the extended ladder has a
sub-threshold tier. **SOURCE-POLICY RED, demonstrated.**

## findings (revision 2)

**F0-8 — SOURCE-POLICY RED. CG-1 is not closed; the world move relocated it rather than removing it.**
Symptom, root cause, evidence and the two-column consequence table are in
`policy_self_consistency (revision 2)` above; the charter-level statement is `_difficulty.md`
§ `findings (revision 2)`, CG-1. In short: `0960d251…` moved from 155 to 95 minutes, which retires
the clash with `air_evt_schedule_change_rights`' first sentence and activates the clash with its
second — *"A move smaller than the brand's threshold gives no right … a traveller who still wants to
cancel is treated as a voluntary cancellation"* — against
`air_ext_cancellation_penalty`'s *"Where the airline has recorded a move on the booking short of the
schedule-change threshold of the fare brand held, the penalty owed is reduced by a tenth."* No
`overwrite` names the base policy. The base reading gives 228.38 / 2353.64 / 1125.31 against gold's
205.54 / 2363.55 / 1129.78.
*Relation to previous revisions.* Revision 1's F0-2 demonstrated the same undeclared conflict on the
at-or-beyond-threshold tier; that demonstration no longer reproduces, and this one replaces it. The
finding is carried forward, not re-opened.

**F0-9 — Observation. The revision-1 findings that are closed, and what closed them.**
F0-3 (CG-2): closed by removal — policy 3 no longer cites `air_baggage_fee`, carries no extras
sentence, binding or factor, so the 45.00 bag line reaches the voucher by no path and the
revision-1 double return is gone. F0-4 (CG-3): closed by declaration — the club uplift is now a
declared override quoting the verbatim base sentence. F0-5 (CG-7): closed — this task's three
affected computations each now carry a genuine `method` factor
(`optional_extras_treatment` rewritten to a brand-rate-per-extra algorithm, `service_fee_basis` new,
`traveller_pool_basis` replacing `named_traveller_share`). F0-6 (CG-9) and F0-7: closed — the release
limit is now per-itinerary with the balance explicitly left on the voucher, and the pool is divided by
the base-fare lines rather than cut by a flat paired share. F0-1: closed, verified above. Each was
re-tested against the artifacts rather than against the reworker's account.

opening world, policy 3 on that world plus both lines, policy 4 on that plus the issue line;
`air_ext_cancellation_penalty.money_collected` still excludes `air_refund_payout`, so the tax write
cannot move the penalty at all, and the tax cap (3663.10, or 3868.64 with the penalty posted first)
does not bind against 674.31 — both orders give `(205.54, 674.31)`, one terminal state; and every
fact consumed is a seeded record or the effect of a preceding write of this task.

**CG-1 is closed, and this is the world that had demonstrated it.** Revision 2 showed the conflict
biting here: `largest_move_minutes = max(70, 45, 95) = 95`, below Economy Classic's threshold of 120
and above zero, so `airline_disruption_share` takes its **sub-threshold** tier, 0.90 — exactly the
tier base `air_evt_schedule_change_rights` legislated for with *"A move smaller than the brand's
threshold gives no right … a traveller who still wants to cancel is treated as a voluntary
cancellation."* That sentence is now quoted verbatim as a `superseded_clause` in
`air_ext_cancellation_penalty.overwrite`, alongside the at-or-beyond-threshold sentence, and both are
replaced by a governing sentence that is present verbatim in the policy's own rule and that covers the
whole ladder: *"What an airline move recorded on the booking does to the penalty owed follows how
large that move was against the schedule-change threshold of the fare brand held, whether or not the
move was large enough to give the traveller a right of its own."*

The final clause is what closes it. Base asserted that a sub-threshold move confers nothing; the
governing sentence says the penalty treatment follows the size of the move *whether or not* the move
confers a right. An agent merging base and extended now finds one rule in force for this quantity, not
two, and the 0.90 tier is the only defensible reading. The revision-2 rival — `disruption_share = 1.00`,
giving 228.38 / 2353.64 / 1125.31 — is no longer defensible, because the sentence it rested on is
declared superseded. The same treatment is given on `air_ext_airline_tax_return` (whose
`repeat_notice_goodwill` keys on notice count) and on `air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit` (whose
`disrupted_penalty_share` keys on cancellation-versus-move), so all three of this task's
notice-reading quantities are covered. **Closed.**

One inherited sentence of that base rule remains unreconciled — *"An airline cancellation of the
segment is always treated as a move beyond the threshold, whatever its recorded minutes"* — and
policy 1 never reads `reason_code`. It is not demonstrable here: all three notices on this booking
carry `reason_code involuntary_schedule_change`, so no `airline_cancellation` row exists to trigger
the divergence. Recorded as charter observation **CG-17**.

## findings (revision 4)

**F0-12 — Observation. R0-1 is closed, and closed in the direction that preserves the business
meaning.** The contradiction was between a rule that said the markup is held back *from the tax lines
returned* and a compute that took it on the lines *as posted*. Moving the compute — rather than
rewriting the rule to describe what the code happened to do — keeps the charter saying what the
business does and makes the number follow. On this world the two readings differ by 1.91 on the tax
return, cascading to 1.67 on the voucher and 0.75 on the release; the scored values move from 674.31 /
2363.55 / 1129.78 to **676.23 / 2361.88 / 1129.03**, and the penalty is rightly untouched because
policy 1 reads no tax figure. Verified by re-deriving the chain from the round-4 text alone and by
confirming that `tax_returned_at` is named in rule, baseline, ladder and compute alike.
*Relation to previous revisions:* this defect was not visible to revisions 1–3 of this audit, which
checked each binding against a quoted rule sentence and found the quotation present; what it did not
check was whether *"held back from the tax lines returned"* and `tax_base * rate` denote the same
figure. The KB audit found it by trying to reach the number from the documents alone. Recorded here as
a limitation this audit is now aware of: a per-binding quotation check can pass while the prose and
the expression disagree about which intermediate a rate acts on.

**F0-13 — Observation. The assembly order is now stated, and on this world it is load-bearing three
times over.** Taking the notice share after the rework loading instead of before gives 196.99 against
205.54; combining the disruption share and the member relief into one rate instead of letting them act
one after another gives 204.34 against 205.54; adding the name-correction carry before the release
share instead of last gives 1122.59 against 1129.03. Each is now settled by a sentence in the policy's
own baseline, in business words, using a stage name the factor sentences also use. A reader who
establishes every tier correctly now reaches the compute's number. *Relation to previous revisions:*
answers the KB audit's finding as it bears on this task's three affected computations, and on the
fourth, which it never demonstrated against.
